newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Members of the China-backed provisional legislature made their first declaration of interests, which showed that 70 percent of members were shareholders or directors of companies.

-- SING TAO -- The Executive Council of the future Special Administrative Region government was trying to influence the Preparatory Committee over how the first SAR legislative council should be produced.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- French Defence Minister Charles Millon said Chinese President Jiang Zemin had said China would sign one of the United Nations conventions on human rights this year.

-- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen urged Taiwan authorities to stop hindering Taiwanese businessmen investing on the mainland so that direct shipping between China and Taiwan could be realised at an early date.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The government said Hong Kong would sign air service agreements with three other countries before the handover, after signing an accord with the United States.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- For the second time in less than four months, Beijing fired a stern warning about signs of overheating in China's stock markets, saying the recent boom in prices could be a trap set by manipulators.
-- Conglomerate Wharf (Holdings) faced potential damages payments of HK$1.0 billion this year from legal action against it in Hong Kong and the United States.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Mass Transit Railway Corp was to withdraw from the HK$30 billion residential commercial project that Swire Properties, Henderson Land, Sun Hung Kai Properties and three other big developers were planning to build nn the waterfront at eastern Kowloon.
-- Taiwan was considering establishing an indicator system to regulate the flow of investment to China. The indicator would reflect political and economic conditions on the mainland.
